chapter: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
title: Planning the J.C. Johnson tribute and bringing back Jazz Train
summary: Rasch describes plans for a tribute, Johnson's wish to revive Jazz Train, Herbie Harper's praise, and a jazz concert on the courthouse lawn.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: They're planning a program for J.C. -- just one for a production, a whole thing, and then they're talking with the people in Wurtsboro, and our friends, the Greenmaryls' and Patti Morrow and Billie Butler, and the people up in Monticello and then in the western part of the county, Elaine, we feel that J.C. could become a catalyst for the county honoring him, but they're doing
something good for the county, giving it a cultural emphasis, which this county so sorely needs.

So we therefore thought -- see, I asked Jay a long time ago if he wanted anything in the world, what do you think you want more than anything else -- and he said he wanted to bring back the Jazz Train, and that was a show that he did'-- and he'll tell you about it -- that was on Broadway, and then toured Europe and played before royalty, and it was really something -- anybody who ever had anything to do with that gets ecstatic, and you just mention it.

Herbie Harper, the choreographer, who lives in the area -- and I think I mentioned his name to you, and he just lights up, when you mentioned Mr. Billie Butler, he just lighted up, and this was something, this show was something that was so unusual and so spectacular, I mean, it did so much for so many.

So this is what we're planning to do, to bring that back in some form or another, intertwined with the story of J.C. However, we now decided that next week we're going to -- this is like a preview thing, so we want everybody in the county to know who J.C. Johnson is, since he's lived here for so many years -- and you know, we want them to know, but we also want to influence the young and old, the black and white; we want to bring together all segments of the community, the eastern part of the county
that doesn't talk to the western part of the county; you know, it's so insane and so stupid -- and so we're all joining forces on this thing to unite everybody in this common purpose.
Now, I don't know if you had a chance to look for the jazz song sheets --

Hugh Brodie is going to play jazz on the courthouse steps, for the art show, for the open air art exhibit on the courthouse lawn a week from Saturday, and we got word that the union is going to pay for the musicians, they're gonna give them the money to do it, see, and they're going to play for two hours, from two to four, a week from Saturday.
That's going to be like a warmup, and they'll be saying things like, 'Who is J.C. Johnson?' -- stuff like that.
